The task input is a single derived AnnData containing only the log1p expression matrix and the projected leiden_res_0.50 label column; every requested quantity (z-scores, raw and BH-adjusted p-values, approximate log2 fold changes for all 17 groups and 23,427 genes) is recomputed from X and label by the solver. The independent implementation executed without answer access and produced a differently-serialized result, corroborating a clean environment. Uninspected coverage residuals: the catalog is a targeted priority-candidate/pattern inspection rather than a byte-exhaustive audit of every packaged test of every library, and integer constants, strings and non-priority files were not literal-scanned; given that the answers were produced by this task's own reference run and are not shipped with any recorded public distribution, and the designed discovery channel (floating-literal comparison against final cells) found nothing, these residuals do not identify a concrete exposure channel and are recorded here rather than held as blockers.

evidence: Provenance chain: the reference de_results.csv is a byte-identical copy of the executed source pipeline's rank_genes_groups.csv (sha 9c1bb8010685c004a69e1705526b244c053073856c2668e1982b375214691a56, 28,207,516 bytes, 398,259 rows = 17 groups x 23,427 genes), recorded from the original scanpy run on the hash-verified 10x inputs with two byte-identical repeatability replays.

The statistical definition matches the installed scanpy 1.12.4 implementation: scanpy/tools/_rank_genes_groups.py ranks all cells once with scipy.stats.rankdata (default method='average' midranks, lines 119-120), then applies std_dev = sqrt(coef * n_active * (n_cells - n_active) * (n_cells + 1) / 12) with coef = 1 when tie_correct=False (line 523), sets non-finite scores to 0 and NaN p-values to 1 before adjustment (lines 449-452, 616), computes p = 2*norm.sf(abs(z)) (line 500), BH via statsmodels multipletests fdr_bh inside each group's per-gene loop (lines 613-619), log2((expm1(mean_group)+1e-9)/(expm1(mean_rest)+1e-9)) (lines 630-635), with defaults reference='rest' (line 663), corr_method='benjamini-hochberg' (line 670), tie_correct=False (line 671), no var mask so all genes are tested.

Cross-implementation equivalence with distinct provenances all pass the grader's seven checks in fresh controls: the byte-copied reference (passed), the scanpy-oracle recomputation from the derived h5ad (sha d5fbe8d2af0855b7c3f3ba19e0ae1cd7a4e0d9bba6034a29dd86eb21b406a0e1, passed), and the independent scipy-primitives implementation with no answer access (sha c757e9b6a702edbfe03a8fe239d1ae83712264530409e29bffc24856d9583536, passed), with the recorded maximum cross-implementation score difference of 3.81e-6 absolute on values up to ~86 remaining inside the 1e-6 relative limit and p-value agreement ~1e-14: the published tolerances are measured equivalence limits for this value chain, not arbitrary slack.

Valid-value acceptance of the permissive boundaries is exercised: the float32 re-serialization probe (all four numeric columns astype float32, underflowing sub-float32 p-values to 0.0, covered by the 1e-8 absolute rule for zeros) and the equal-score tie permutation probe both pass all seven checks, consistent with the grader code (np.diff(block_scores) > 0 accepts non-increasing order; both ascending label orders enumerated by ascending_orders()). These controls establish that the accepted tolerance does not silently reject any representable valid encoding the public text admits.

Wrong-answer rejection at the boundaries through well-formed CSVs: the 2e-5 score nudge on 12 rows fails only wilcoxon_scores; the single-row LFC replacement fails only logfoldchanges; the 10x pval on a moderate p (0.0508 to 0.5018) fails only pvals; the 1000x clipped padj on group 1 (19,227 rows) fails only pvals_adj; the unknown-gene insertion is rejected on identity/coverage. Identity gates were verified against the trusted input via the grader's load_input_facts() using BIOTASKS_TRUSTED_INPUT_DIR, not the reference's row inventory alone.

The row alignment is bijective on (group, names): the grader requires sub_groups == label_set, sub_genes == set(var_names), exactly one row per group per gene, matching row counts and no duplicate keys, so all dependent outputs (scores, pvals, pvals_adj, logfoldchanges of the same (group, gene)) are consistently aligned under a single identity mapping anchored to the immutable input.
comparisons.rationale: The single output path de_results.csv is scientifically equivalent to the recorded reference under the published contract, and the contract is a faithful encoding of the reference computation. The comparison aligns rows on the bijective (group, names) key, checks the entity population against the immutable trusted input rather than reference-only sets, applies column-specific measured equivalence limits (1e-6 abs/rel for scores and logfoldchanges; 1e-8 abs/1e-6 rel for p-values, with zeros meaningful rather than treated as missing), and enforces ordering as group-block contiguity, ascending group block order (both documented conventions) and descending scores with explicit tie-order freedom. Both directions of the equivalence have dedicated executed evidence: three provenance-distinct correct implementations (recorded reference, scanpy oracle, independent primitive implementation without answer access) are accepted, and each scientific column has a dedicated wrong_solution probe rejected at a magnitude above its tolerance while all other columns pass. Dependencies between outputs (BH adjustment depends on raw p-values within each group; identity depends on the trusted input) are respected: the per-group padj probe changes only group 1's adjusted values and the pvals probe only the raw column, so dependent checks isolate their targets, and the coverage probe cascades correctly into all value checks.

source_coverage.rationale: Every source_operations call site appears exactly once in the materialization candidate's operation_coverage ledger, and the single retained endpoint is the notebook's sole independent quantitative statistical result: the per-cluster one-vs-rest Wilcoxon marker table (call-300-0, sc.tl.rank_genes_groups(groupby='leiden_res_0.50', method='wilcoxon') on all genes), exported by the source's own helper sc.get.rank_genes_groups_df. The endpoint is recovered completely (17 groups x 23,427 genes = 398,259 rows, matching the reference's distinct names count of 23,427 and row count of 398,259, so no HVG-style truncation occurred) and is requested in full as solver work; only the recorded leiden_res_0.50 clustering realization is supplied as data with an explicit derivation and barcode-exact alignment, which is the permitted supplied-intermediate pattern rather than a withheld answer. Exclusions were independently reviewed against the source narrative, plan.json and exports.py and accepted with source-backed reasons: QC metrics, scrublet doublet scores and HVG annotation are diagnostics that do not modify X or the DE gene population (scrublet is never filtered on in the source, which only re-plots predicted_doublet and doublet_score; DE covers the full filtered gene set); adata.layers['counts'] is a provenance intermediate not consumed by DE; the default-resolution Leiden and the 0.02/2.00 resolution solutions are alternative stochastic single realizations whose only consumers are plots and the curated manual annotation; cell_type_lvl1 is a deterministic .map() relabeling of a curated annotation dictionary over another clustering realization, consumed only by plots and the per-cell export; UMAP is a 2D visualization embedding. No eligible scientific branch of the converted source is missing and no described scientific check is only partially present. Every operation-coverage claim was checked against the source code, including the DE all-genes claim verified by the reference's 23,427 distinct names against the full filtered gene set.
remaining_validation: After the correct reclassification of the equal-score tie-permutation probe to valid_alternative, the structural ordering check has no dedicated executed wrong_solution probe (the original probe's mutation was contract-compliant and never established ordering rejection). Its logic is directly verifiable in the grader source (block-count mismatch for interleaving, allowed-orders check for permutation, np.diff > 0 for ascending scores) and all four scientific checks retain dedicated negative probes; a residual validation-coverage note, not a defect of the current candidate.

Repeatability evidence is limited to repeated runs of the recorded pipeline (byte-identical exports on two replays) and does not establish cross-platform reproducibility of the upstream stochastic steps; accepted because those stochastic realizations are excluded from the graded contract and supplied as recorded data.

The tolerance bounds are demonstrated equivalence limits from the three executed implementations, not proof that every future environment produces values within them; any reference revision would require its own validation.
